newsitem.title: FINLAND: Helsinki corrects down as Nokia fails to hold gain.
newsitem.headline: Helsinki corrects down as Nokia fails to hold gain.

text.p: Shares fell overall on Friday in a U.S.-led correction as Nokia failed to hold Thursday's gains and forestries were weak, but the market was bolstered by insurers and Outokumpu, brokers said.
The HEX recoiled from Thursday's records and closed 1.04 percent lower at 2,873.00 points, fractionally ahead on the week but still about 15 percent up on the year.
Nokia closed at 306.00, down 6.00 markka, accounting for a quarter of total trade which at 680 million markka was quiet by recent standards butstill much heavier than last year's normal levels.
Even facing a downward correction, analysts said the bourse may yet have momentum to take it above 3,000 before summer.
"We have the view that spring will be difficult ... there would still be a two percent rise in a month from now, but April would be a tough time," said Aktia Bank analyst Ritva Ojala.
For the full year Aktia expects an 11 percent rise, and the HEX will hit 3,000 points this summer, she said.
Insurers continued to climb on speculation of restructuring, and metals and minings group Outokumpu rose on recommendations following gains fuelled by firmer metal prices, brokers said.

Insurance majors Sampo and Pohjola both touched life highs. Pohjola hit 160.00 markka, but closed off at 158.00, still up 5.00 markka or over three percent. Sampo closed at its new 500.00 markka all-time high, up 20.00 markka.
Recent mergers in the Swedish finance sector have fuelled expectations of similar types of arrangements in Finland.
Pharmaceuticals group Orion fell after in-line results -- down 8.00 at 180.00 -- mainly on profit-taking from strong gains ahead of a satisfactory result, brokers said.
Next week could be livelier with fewer people on winter holidays, they said.
